# `legacy-format-method`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: correctness · Profile: none · Default: warning · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports a `format` method with the pre-0.15 `(self, comptime fmt, options,
writer)` signature, which `std.fmt` no longer calls.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Since Zig 0.15 `std.fmt` calls a type's `format` method only for the `{f}`
specifier, and only with the signature
`format(self, writer: *std.Io.Writer) std.Io.Writer.Error!void`. A method still
declared `format(self, comptime fmt: []const u8, options: std.fmt.FormatOptions,
writer: anytype)` is never called: `{}` and `{any}` print the value's fields
instead, and `{f}` fails to compile against the old signature. The method's
custom output is silently gone until it is migrated.

## When it fires

On a function named `format` with four parameters whose second is
`comptime name: []const u8` and whose third is typed `FormatOptions` (any
path) or `fmt.Options`. The writer parameter may have any type. The finding
points at the method name and carries related information on the two
parameters to remove, with the reminder that callers format the value with
`{f}`. There is no automatic fix: the body may use the format string or
options, and every `{}` that formats the type has to change too.
`prefer-typed-io-parameter` does not also report the writer parameter of such
a method while this rule is enabled.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

const Point = struct {
    x: i32,

    pub fn format(self: Point, comptime fmt: []const u8, options: std.fmt.Options, writer: *std.Io.Writer) !void {
        _ = fmt;
        _ = options;
        try writer.print("({d})", .{self.x});
    }
};
```

Reference: <https://ziglang.org/download/0.15.1/release-notes.html>
